A patient presents with a 1-year history of burning dysesthesias in the neck and arms and paresthesias/numbness in the hands, progressing over the past 3 months to include bilateral hand weakness. While the brain MRI is pending, the *high pretest probability* of Chiari I is justified: it is the most common cause of non-traumatic, non-tumoral syringomyelia — particularly when the syrinx spans cervical and upper thoracic levels and presents with dissociated sensory loss and distal weakness.
